summary: Bajracharya specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. Educated at Tribhuvan University, HTW Berlin, and Metropolia University of Applied Sciences, he held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018) and Heidelberg University (attested 2023).
Manilal Patel was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Marburg, where he studied under Johannes Nobel.

Manish Sinha works in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at Magadh University in 1999, where he became Professor in 1996 and Head of Department (2018–2021).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Akkhachat completed a B.A. at Ramkhamhaeng University (2007–2009) and a Ph.D. at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (2017–2022). He lectured at Nakhon Ratchasima Rajabhat University in 2013.

Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, Bhalerao studied at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth. She became Associate Professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth in 2004 and visiting faculty at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

Manlio Iofrida is a philosopher who studied at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore (~1970–1974). He held posts at the University of Pisa (~1984–1992) and the University of Bologna (~1992).

Manshi Kiyozawa (1863–1903) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa. He served as the first dean and founding president of Otani University (1901–1902).

Manu Leumann (1889–1977) was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Strasbourg under Albert Thumb. He worked at Thesaurus Linguae Latinae and was ordinary Professor at the University of Zurich from 1927 to 1959.

id: P:Manuel Antonio Ato del Avellanal Carrera
summary: Carrera specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Nava Nalanda Mahavihara and SOAS University of London, and later lectured at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru (2020) and Universidad del Pacífico (2023).

Manuel Sassmann is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Stuttgart and Heidelberg University, and has served as a Research Fellow at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

id: P:Manuel de la Revilla y Moreno
summary: Manuel de la Revilla y Moreno (1846–1881) was a philosopher who studied under Francisco García Ayuso at Complutense University of Madrid. He later served there as Professor of Literary History from 1876.

Marbury Bladen Ogle (1879–1964) was a classicist and linguist who studied at Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield and Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve. He held professorships at the University of Vermont, Ohio State University, and the University of Minnesota.

Marc Aurel Stein (1862–1943) was an archaeologist, Indologist, and Central Asian specialist. He earned his Ph.D. at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and held positions at Punjab University, Oriental College, and the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1929).
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Lausanne under Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.
Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein.
Marcel Cohen (1884–1974) was a French linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the University of Paris and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1919–1954).

Marcel Granet (1884–1940) was a French sinologist and religious studies scholar educated at the École Normale Supérieure under Édouard Chavannes and Émile Durkheim. He held professorships at EPHE, INALCO, and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises.

Marcel Hofinger (1913–1997) was a Belgian scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Étienne Lamotte at KU Leuven, where he later became an ordinary Professor in 1959, and taught at Université catholique de Louvain (~1947–1983).

Marcel Mauss (1872–1950) was a French scholar of religion and philosophy mentored by Émile Durkheim. He served as Directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1914–1940) and held the Chair of Sociology at the Collège de France (1931–1941).

Marcelle Lalou (1890–1967) was a French Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her Ph.D. at EPHE. She served as Directeur d’études at EPHE (1938–1963) and was chief editor of the Journal Asiatique (1950–1966).
